answer.summary: Rahul Vohra’s Switch log tracks what he actually works on: whenever he changes tasks, he sends a Slack message beginning “TS:” plus a few words describing the task. Reviewing the entries at week’s end shows where his time went, and the log can be graphed or charted.

sections.heading: How the Switch log works
sections.content: Vohra calls it the “Switch log.” Rather than relying on a calendar—which records what he planned to do—he records his trail of work. Each time he switches tasks, he Slack-DMs his executive assistant (or uses Slackbot / another place to capture it) with “TS:” followed by a few words describing the task. He says this lets him choose what to work on and for how long, then review at the end of the week where his time actually went; the entries can also be graphed or charted.

sections.heading: Caveat and example of its use
sections.content: He is not suggesting skipping meetings or one-on-ones; the technique is for tracking discretionary work. Reviewing the log showed him that he spent only 5% of his time recruiting when he thought he perhaps should spend 20–30% or more, and only 6–7% on product, design, technology, and marketing—areas where he believed he was strongest. That insight helped him rethink how to allocate his time.
